title: Trigonometric ratios in a right triangle

widget.instructions: Drag corner B (or use the slider) to change the angle, and mark θ at A or B to see which sides are opposite and adjacent.

steps.text: This is a right triangle with the right angle at C. The longest side, AB, is across from the right angle: it is always the **hypotenuse**.
θ is the angle at A. The side across from θ is **opposite**. The other side that touches θ is **adjacent**.
Now move θ to corner B. Watch the labels: opposite and adjacent swap places, while the hypotenuse stays the same.
Back at A, the ratios: sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent. Watch them change as θ sweeps.
Your turn: drag corner B or use the slider, and mark θ at A or at B. Say which side is adjacent before you look at the labels.

args.text: Your turn: mark θ, then name the sides.

widget.instructions: A lamp shines straight down and straight across. Drag the vector's tip (or use the slider) and watch its shadows on the axes.

steps.text: Here is a vector of length r at θ above the x-axis. Its shadow on the x-axis (lamp overhead) and on the y-axis (lamp to the side) are its two components.
The x-shadow touches the angle θ at the origin: it is **adjacent**. So x = r cos θ.
The y-shadow sits across from θ: it is **opposite**. So y = r sin θ. Sweep θ and watch the two shadows trade length.

recap.text: Recap: the hypotenuse is across from the right angle, the opposite side is across from θ, and the adjacent side touches θ. sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.

accessibility.altText: A right triangle ABC with the right angle at C and the angle θ marked at A. Each side is labelled opposite, adjacent or hypotenuse.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use the angle slider and the Mark θ at A or Mark θ at B buttons; the description below the figure names each side.
